trends.label: Software postings rebound, led by senior and AI-titled roles
trends.finding: US software development postings rose almost 15% after late February 2025, while overall postings fell 7%. They are still 27.5% below the pre-pandemic level. Senior roles accounted for 71% of the increase from May 2025 to May 2026, and jobs with AI in the title accounted for 37%.
trends.implication: A senior candidate with real AI-feature work is aimed at the part of the market that is growing. Lead with seniority and AI evidence.

trends.label: Software is the most senior-skewed job category
trends.finding: In Q1 2026, 69.3% of software development postings were senior-level and 4.5% were entry-level, the highest and lowest shares of any sector Hiring Lab tracks. US senior postings overall were up 14.7% year over year in May 2026.
trends.implication: Level deflation pressure falls mostly on juniors. A six-year engineer should present at senior or lead scope (owned systems, decisions, mentoring), not as mid-level.

trends.label: AI skills are now listed in most tech postings
trends.finding: Dice found at least one AI skill in 73% of US tech postings in May 2026, up from 15% in January 2024. Postings with AI in the title rose 173% year over year in Q1 2026. Indeed found that tech postings mentioning AI were about 45% above February 2020 levels at the end of 2025, while all tech postings were 34% below.
trends.implication: Name concrete AI skills (LLM APIs, agents, evals, coding assistants) in résumé text that ATS keyword filters can match. Leaving them out now reads as a gap.

trends.label: AI-assisted coding is expected, and verification is what distinguishes candidates
trends.finding: 80% of developers use AI tools, but only 29% trust their accuracy. 45% say their top frustration is answers that are 'almost right', and 66% spend more time fixing near-miss AI code. Shopify's CEO made 'reflexive AI usage' a baseline expectation and added it to performance reviews.
trends.implication: Show that you use agents with controls: CI gates, review policy, tests. That combination of speed and verification is the criterion employers are looking for.

trends.label: Interviews are splitting into AI-allowed rounds and no-AI rounds
trends.finding: Canva requires candidates to use AI in coding interviews and scores how they handle ambiguity and fix flaws in AI-generated code. Meta piloted AI-assisted coding rounds. Karat reports that 62% of organisations still ban AI in interviews, and that take-homes and automated tests lose criterion fastest because only the output is visible. Karat's US figures: take-homes used by 45% of companies, live interviews by 79%.
trends.implication: Prepare for both formats. Portfolio write-ups about how you verify agent output pre-empt the AI-allowed round. Expect fewer take-homes and more live or in-person rounds.

trends.label: AI screening, application floods and fraud
trends.finding: Greenhouse's 2025 survey: 41% of US job seekers admit using prompt injections in résumés, 22% of hiring managers have caught one, and 65% have caught deceptive AI use. 39% of hiring managers are running more in-person interviews to verify authenticity, and only 21% of recruiters are very confident their AI isn't rejecting qualified people. Gartner predicts that 1 in 4 candidate profiles worldwide could be fake by 2028.
trends.implication: Verifiable identity and work carry more weight: a consistent LinkedIn profile, a real GitHub history, a personal domain and named references. Never use hidden-text tricks.

trends.label: Fully remote is a minority, and hybrid is tightening
trends.finding: Among US AI-engineering postings that state a work model, 32% are fully remote, 48% hybrid and 20% on-site. In the UK, software development has the highest remote/hybrid share of any occupation (48%), but typical hybrid roles now require 2.3 office days a week, up 0.6 days in two years.
trends.implication: A remote-only search narrows the pool sharply. Target remote-first companies and AI-engineering roles, where remote shares are higher, and say 'US citizen, remote, open to travel' up front.

trends.label: AI engineering is the fastest-growing engineering segment
trends.finding: LinkedIn: AI Engineers' share of software engineering hires is 14x the 2019 level and 10x the 2022 level, and transitions into generative-AI engineer roles have grown about ninefold since 2021, though they are still under 1% of job switches. The Pragmatic Engineer reports many large tech companies have 50–100% more AI-engineering listings than a year earlier.
trends.implication: Moving from product engineer to AI product engineer is the highest-leverage repositioning available to a TypeScript product engineer.

trends.label: Hiring outcomes favour Python, cloud and data over classic web skills
trends.finding: The top skills among US software engineering hires (2021–2025) are Python, AWS, SQL, JavaScript and React. The fastest-growing are AI, Tailwind CSS, Azure Databricks, Google BigQuery and Azure SQL. Five years earlier, JavaScript, CSS and HTML led.
trends.implication: Pair the TypeScript/React core with visible Python, cloud and data work. Pure frontend positioning is weakening.

trends.label: TypeScript became GitHub's most-used language
trends.finding: In August 2025, TypeScript passed Python and JavaScript in monthly contributors on GitHub. It added more than one million contributors, which GitHub links to AI-assisted development and typed defaults in frameworks.
trends.implication: A TypeScript-first profile is mainstream and fits AI-assisted workflows well. Frame it as an asset in agent-heavy teams.

trends.label: Forward deployed engineering became a hot AI-era role
trends.finding: The Pragmatic Engineer documents startups and scaleups hiring forward deployed engineers in large numbers. These are software engineers embedded with customers who also work on the core product, a role Palantir pioneered and AI companies have adopted. Its 2026 market report says AI and FDE roles are surging while mobile and frontend demand drops.
trends.implication: Integration-heavy, customer-facing builders are in demand. The candidate's API emulator, third-party integration work and stakeholder-facing tech-lead experience map directly to it.

trends.label: The AI pay premium grows with seniority
trends.finding: Levels.fyi measured the AI-engineer premium over non-AI peers in 2025 at 6.2% for entry level, 11.9% for engineer, 14.2% for senior and 18.7% for staff. Axial Search reports a $176,000 median posted salary across 43,480 US AI-engineering postings in 2026.
trends.implication: For a senior engineer, credible AI positioning is worth real money, and the premium grows at staff level.

trends.label: Cold applications convert poorly, and warm paths matter more
trends.finding: The Pragmatic Engineer reports experienced engineers who only get interviews when they know someone at the company. Ashby data shows referrals are about 1% of applications but convert to interviews at 40%. Greenhouse reports recruiters spending up to half their week filtering junk applications.
trends.implication: Spend a meaningful share of search time on referrals, communities (AI Engineer meetups, OSS maintainers) and direct outreach to hiring managers.

trends.label: Kubernetes is the default production platform, including for AI inference
trends.finding: CNCF's 2025 survey: 82% of container users run Kubernetes in production, and 66% of organisations running generative-AI models use Kubernetes for inference.
trends.implication: Kubernetes appears as an assumed requirement in many senior backend and platform roles. Hands-on proof closes the most common gap at moderate cost.

universalCriteria.label: Quantified impact
universalCriteria.why: Hiring managers use numbers to judge both the size of the outcome and whether the candidate can measure their own work.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Give each role two or three bullets with a measured result (latency, cost, conversion, incidents, time saved), with the baseline stated.

universalCriteria.label: Title that matches the posting
universalCriteria.why: Jobscan found a 10.6x higher interview rate when the résumé title matched the target title, and 55%+ of recruiters filter by title.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Keep résumé variants whose headline uses the exact posted title (Senior Software Engineer / AI Engineer / Product Engineer) where it is truthful.

universalCriteria.label: Public proof that runs
universalCriteria.why: Reviewers clone repos and follow READMEs, and AI-generated portfolios have made verifiable work more valuable.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Pin one to three repos with a clean quickstart, tests, CI badge and a short design note.

universalCriteria.label: Disciplined AI-assisted workflow
universalCriteria.why: Employers expect AI use but distrust unverified output, and AI-allowed interviews score how candidates catch AI mistakes.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Write up the AGENTS.md policy, the CI gates, and one concrete bug the gates caught.

universalCriteria.label: Referrals and warm introductions
universalCriteria.why: Referred applicants convert to interviews at about 40% in Ashby data, far above the flood of cold AI-assisted applications.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Keep a target list of 20–30 companies and ask former colleagues, OSS contacts and meetup peers for introductions.

universalCriteria.label: Consistent, optimised LinkedIn profile
universalCriteria.why: 73.3% of recruiters always or often check LinkedIn, an optimised profile came with a 2.2x interview rate, and authenticity checks are rising because of candidate fraud.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Use the same title, dates and headline metrics as the résumé, with links to the portfolio and GitHub.

universalCriteria.label: Written reasoning (ADRs, write-ups)
universalCriteria.why: Hiring managers ask candidates to defend architecture and model choices, and writing shows judgement that code alone doesn't.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Publish two or three short decision records or blog posts (for example, why OpenTofu, or the LLM proxy's routing policy).

universalCriteria.label: Short tailored cover note
universalCriteria.why: Jobscan measured a 3.4x higher interview rate when a cover letter was included.
universalCriteria.howToDemonstrate: Write three or four sentences linking one portfolio case study to the company's product problem.

resumeRules.rule: Mirror the target job title in the headline and summary.
resumeRules.why: A matching title came with a 10.6x higher interview rate in Jobscan's 2025 data.

resumeRules.rule: Write the posting's hard-skill keywords literally (for example 'Kubernetes', 'LLM APIs', 'TypeScript'), not only synonyms.
resumeRules.why: Over 99.7% of surveyed recruiters use ATS filters, and 76.4% start by filtering on skills. Workday, the most common Fortune 500 ATS, is used by over 39% of them.

resumeRules.rule: Use a single-column layout with no tables, text boxes, graphics or headers/footers holding key data. Submit PDF or DOCX.
resumeRules.why: Greenhouse's support documentation lists layout elements and oversized files (over 2.5MB) as causes of failed résumé parsing.

resumeRules.rule: Two pages are fine for a senior engineer, but page one must carry the case.
resumeRules.why: In ResumeGo's 2018 simulation, recruiters were 2.3x as likely to prefer two-page résumés, though the study has limits. Ladders' eye-tracking found the first scan lasts about 7.4 seconds and focuses on titles and subheads.

resumeRules.rule: Make the top third do the work: title, a two-line summary with the strongest proof, then the most relevant role.
resumeRules.why: Recruiters' initial scan focuses on job titles and section heads in a few seconds.

resumeRules.rule: Use the bullet formula verb + system/scope + measured outcome + how.
resumeRules.why: Orosz advises numbers and specifics because they show impact and the ability to quantify it.

resumeRules.rule: Weight recent work. Go deep on the last 5–6 years and compress older work.
resumeRules.why: Recruiters cited in Jobscan's report focus on recent career accomplishments, roughly the last 15 years at most.

resumeRules.rule: Link LinkedIn, GitHub and a portfolio, and keep them consistent with the résumé.
resumeRules.why: 73.3% of recruiters check LinkedIn, and rising fraud makes cross-checkable identity a trust criterion.

resumeRules.rule: Never hide keywords or prompt-injection text.
resumeRules.why: 22% of hiring managers have already caught hidden prompt injections, and 65% have caught deceptive AI use. Getting caught ends the candidacy.

resumeRules.rule: Name AI tools concretely and pair them with how output is verified.
resumeRules.why: Most tech postings now list AI skills, but employers distrust unverified AI output and test verification in interviews.

resumeRules.rule: Include a short tailored cover letter when the form allows one.
resumeRules.why: Jobscan measured a 3.4x higher interview rate with a cover letter.

resumeRules.rule: Link only repos that run from a clean clone.
resumeRules.why: Hiring managers clone public projects and follow the README. A broken repo counts against the candidate.

recommendations.gap: No public evals or AI case study
recommendations.move: Build an eval harness for the LLM proxy or one Geviti-style feature: read 20–50 traces, write a failure taxonomy, add binary checks and one judge validated against human labels, and publish a case study with before/after numbers.
recommendations.payoff: Directly addresses the top AI-engineer screening question ('how did you know it worked?') and opens the AI product engineer role.

recommendations.gap: LLM work lacks cost and latency numbers
recommendations.move: Instrument the LLM proxy to record tokens, cost per request, p50/p95 latency and routing decisions per provider, then publish a dashboard screenshot and a short write-up.
recommendations.payoff: Turns an existing project into evidence of production AI work and pre-empts token-cost interview exercises.

recommendations.move: Re-mine One Origin and Geviti work for measurable outcomes (latency, release frequency, incidents, user counts, cost) and rewrite every bullet with the verb + scope + metric formula.
recommendations.payoff: Raises résumé conversion across every role at near-zero cost.

recommendations.move: Deploy the open-source API emulator to a managed Kubernetes cluster with OpenTofu plus a Helm chart, with health checks, autoscaling and an ADR. Skip the CKA unless targeting platform roles.
recommendations.payoff: Converts the biggest keyword gap into truthful, demonstrable experience. Kubernetes runs in production at 82% of container users.

recommendations.move: Only if targeting enterprise or contractor roles: build one small Spring Boot service (for example a Java client or adapter for the emulator) with tests and CI. Otherwise deprioritise it, because Java demand is steady, not growing.
recommendations.payoff: Passes Java keyword filters for enterprise roles. Low return for AI or startup targets.

recommendations.move: Port one OpenTofu stack to a second cloud and write up the differences. Consider a single associate-level cert only when applying to Azure-heavy enterprises, because ATS keyword filters match certification names but senior hiring weighs hands-on work.
recommendations.payoff: Moves from single-cloud to multi-cloud credibility. Azure skills are among the fastest-growing among SWE hires.

recommendations.gap: AI-assisted workflow is invisible to employers
recommendations.move: Publish the AGENTS.md policy and CI gates as a blog post or README section ('how I ship with coding agents safely'), including a defect the gates caught.
recommendations.payoff: Directly matches what AI-allowed interviews score (verifying AI output) and differentiates from unverified 'vibe coding'.

recommendations.gap: Limited public OSS footprint in the AI tooling ecosystem
recommendations.move: Make two or three meaningful contributions to an eval or observability library the candidate already uses (bug fixes, TypeScript SDK improvements, docs with examples).
recommendations.payoff: Public, verifiable proof in exactly the area AI teams hire for, plus warm contacts with maintainers.

recommendations.move: Write the eval harness or one small FastAPI service in Python and list Python credibly alongside TypeScript.
recommendations.payoff: Python is in 62% of AI-engineering postings and is the top skill among SWE hires.

recommendations.move: Add an event stream (for example, webhook events from the emulator published to a Kafka-compatible broker) with one consumer service, documented in an ADR. Treat it as a low priority.
recommendations.payoff: Clears keyword filters for event-driven backend roles. A smaller gap, so a smaller return.

recommendations.move: Build a target list of 20–30 remote-friendly AI or product companies and ask former colleagues and OSS or meetup contacts for introductions before applying.
recommendations.payoff: Referrals convert to interviews at about 40% in Ashby's data, versus the noise of cold AI-assisted applications.

recommendations.move: Keep three résumé variants (Senior Software Engineer, Senior Full-Stack Engineer, AI Product Engineer) whose headlines match posted titles truthfully.
recommendations.payoff: Title match came with a 10.6x interview-rate lift in Jobscan's data.
